chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, both together, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi, from Salih ibn Khalid, from Yaman al-Tammar, who said:

We were seated in the presence of Abu ‘Abd Allah (عليه السلام), and he said to us: “Indeed, for the Master of this affair there shall be a ghaybah (occultation); the one who holds fast to his religion during it is like one stripping al-qatad thorn-bush.”
Then he said, indicating like this with his hand: “Which of you can grasp the thorns of al-qatad with his hand?”

Then he lowered his head for a long while, then said: “Indeed, for the Master of this affair there shall be a ghaybah (occultation), so let the servant have taqwa of Allah and hold fast to his religion.”

key_terms.الْخَارِطِ: one who strips or draws along painfully
key_terms.الْقَتَادِ: a thorny desert bush used here as a metaphor for difficulty
key_terms.الْمُتَمَسِّكُ: the one who holds firmly and remains steadfast
key_terms.بِدِينِهِ: to his religion; meaning adherence to the faith
key_terms.صَاحِبِ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the Master of this affair, referring to the divinely appointed Imam
key_terms.غَيْبَةً: occultation; the period in which the Imam is hidden from public view
key_terms.فَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ: so let him have taqwa of Allah; let him be God-conscious and wary of disobedience

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) describe holding fast to religion during the ghaybah?
ai.summary: This hadith foretells the ghaybah (occultation) of the Sahib al-Amr and describes steadfastness in religion during that period as extremely difficult. Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) exhorts the believers to maintain taqwa and cling firmly to their din despite the hardship of the time.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya and Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Sayrafi, from Salih Bin Khalid, from Yaman Al Tammar who said,

‘We were seated in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to us: ‘For the Master<sup>asws</sup> of this command there would be an Occultation. Being attached to his<sup>asws</sup> Religion would be like entering into the thorny bush’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Like this!’ – by his<sup>asws</sup> hand. So, which one of you would like to touch a branch of thorns?’

Then he<sup>asws</sup> was silent for a while, then said: ‘For the Master<sup>asws</sup> of this command there would be an Occultation, so let a servant fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and let him attach with his<sup>asws</sup> Religion’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya and al-Hassan ibn Muhammad both have narrated from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi from Salih ibn Khalid from Yaman al-Tammar who has said the following.

“Once we were in the presence of abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) and he said to us, “The in charge of this task (Leadership with Divine Authority) will disappear from public sight. At that time following one’s religion would like wiping the thorns of cactus plant with one’s bare.
The Imam (a.s.) made certain hand gestures. Who among you is ready to hold in his hands a branch of cactus?

He then remained quite for a little while and then said, “The in charge of this task (Leadership with Divine Authority) will disappear from public sight. A servant (of Allah) must maintain piety before Him and hold fast to His religion,”
